report.summary: Reviewed 5 findings: handoff-data-loss (high, confirmed), silent-exception-swallowing (medium, needs-evidence), live_egress_reuse (medium, needs-evidence), containment-guarantee-unverified (high, needs-evidence), spectral-truncation-mismatch (medium, narrowed). Proposed 5 work items.
risks: handoff-data-loss may break downstream consumers; fix requires schema change and consumer audit.
containment-guarantee-unverified: missing functions may exist elsewhere; full file scan needed.
live_egress_reuse: if live_egress_seats duplicates logic, consistency bugs may arise.
silent-exception-swallowing in close() may mask corruption; need to inspect and possibly add logging.
spectral-truncation-mismatch could cause index errors if component_count > 8; downstream code must be checked.
todos: Audit all consumers of handoff field to see if they expect structured data.
Inspect close() in ledger.py for exception handling.
Inspect live_egress_seats in session.py to see if it delegates.
Scan attempt.py and containment.py for missing functions.
Search for code consuming eigenvalues to check for index assumptions.

items.title: Fix handoff-data-loss by extending REPORT_SCHEMA to allow structured handoff
items.why_now: Current strict schema strips all non-notes fields, which can silently break downstream consumers that expect structured data from churn.py or other sources. This is a data integrity issue at the system boundary.

steps.do: Modify REPORT_SCHEMA to allow an optional 'handoff' object with additionalProperties: true, or change handoff to be an object with a 'notes' string and other optional fields.
steps.verified_by: Run existing tests; ensure no regression. Write a test that submits a report with structured handoff and verifies it is preserved.

steps.do: Audit all code that reads the handoff field from a report. Use grep for '.handoff' or 'handoff' in Python files.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'handoff' daedalus/ --include='*.py' and list all accesses. If any access fields other than 'notes', confirm they are now supported.

items.assumption: We assume the REPORT_SCHEMA is defined in a schema file; path unknown. If no downstream consumers exist beyond the human reviewer, severity may be lower.

items.title: Verify containment guarantees by locating missing functions
items.why_now: command_gate's docstring claims guarantees that depend on external functions not visible in provided chunks. If these functions are missing, the containment guarantee is unsupported, which is a critical security issue.

steps.do: Search for 'Job Object', 'refusal_attestation', '_remove_gate_tmpdir' in daedalus/spine/attempt.py and daedalus/spine/containment.py.
steps.verified_by: grep -n 'Job Object\|refusal_attestation\|_remove_gate_tmpdir' daedalus/spine/attempt.py daedalus/spine/containment.py. If found, verify definitions; if not, document as missing.

steps.do: If missing, add the necessary functions or update docstring to remove unsupported claims.
steps.verified_by: Run tests; ensure containment tests pass.

items.assumption: We assume the functions are either defined elsewhere or need to be added. Full file scan is required.

items.title: Inspect live_egress_seats for duplication with available_providers
items.why_now: If live_egress_seats duplicates logic from available_providers, there is a risk of inconsistency. This is a medium-severity maintenance issue.

steps.do: Open daedalus/council/session.py and inspect live_egress_seats implementation.
steps.verified_by: Read lines 30-60 (or search for 'def live_egress_seats'). Check if it calls available_providers or provider_health.

steps.do: If it duplicates logic, refactor to delegate to available_providers.
steps.verified_by: Run existing tests; ensure behavior unchanged.

items.assumption: We assume the file path is correct and the function is defined within the first 60 lines.

items.title: Inspect close() in ledger.py for silent exception swallowing
items.why_now: If close() catches all sqlite3.Error and does nothing, it may mask corruption or resource leaks. Although common practice, it should be verified.

steps.verified_by: Read the close() method; check if it logs or re-raises exceptions. If it silently ignores, add logging.

items.assumption: We assume ledger.py is at daedalus/spine/ledger.py and has a close() method.

items.title: Fix spectral-truncation-mismatch by adjusting truncation or downstream code
items.why_now: If component_count > 8, eigenvalues list is truncated, potentially causing index errors in downstream consumers that assume one eigenvalue per component.

steps.do: Search for code that consumes topology.eigenvalues and check if it uses len(eigenvalues) or component_count.
If downstream assumes component_count, either remove truncation or ensure downstream uses len(eigenvalues).
steps.verified_by: Run tests; ensure no index errors.

items.assumption: We assume topology.eigenvalues is used somewhere; path unknown.
